clue.text: Purchase notes that have different numbers?

definitions.text: Purchase notes that have different numbers?

parts.words: Purchase notes that have different numbers?
parts.note: banknotes buy things and each one carries its own serial number, while 'different numbers' also hints at denominations

explanation.surface: A query about buying sheet music in varied numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' and 'numbers' read as music, but they are banknotes and their serial numbers or values.
explanation.definitionFit: Banknotes are printed money used for buying, each with a unique serial.

clue.text: Call for silence once the conduit has been laid

definitions.meaning: an order to be quiet, as a bosun's whistle once signalled lights out

definitions.text: once the conduit has been laid
definitions.meaning: a pipe that has been laid is a pipe put down

explanation.surface: A plumber asks for quiet when the job is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means 'be quiet'; read literally it is a tube placed in position.

clue.text: Sign an autograph book giving fictitious identity?

definitions.text: Sign an autograph book giving fictitious identity?

parts.words: Sign an autograph book giving fictitious identity?
parts.note: signing a book means writing your name with a pen, and an author's invented name is a writer's alias

explanation.surface: A fan signs a book with a false name.
explanation.definitionFit: An author's assumed name is the one written by the pen, a literary pseudonym.

clue.text: Something that is very hard to sway

definitions.meaning: stone is a byword for hardness
to move to and fro, as a cradle does

explanation.surface: An unpersuadable person is hard to win over.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone is the type of something hard; rocking is swaying back and forth.

clue.text: See 1
Not overmanned, as much of Africa is?

definitions.text: Not overmanned, as much of Africa is?

parts.words: Not overmanned, as much of Africa is?
parts.note: the opposite of having too many people, as vast thinly settled regions are

explanation.surface: A remark on staffing compared with sparse African populations.
explanation.definitionFit: Having too few inhabitants is the reverse of being overmanned.

clue.text: Hardly what the prospects are these days in railway circles!

definitions.text: Hardly what the prospects are these days in railway circles!

parts.words: Hardly what the prospects are these days in railway circles!
parts.note: railway prospects are said to be anything but bright and hopeful

explanation.surface: A gloomy comment on the railway industry's future.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright, hopeful prospects are called pink-tinted, the opposite of gloomy.

clue.text: A little matter quite free of charge

definitions.text: A little matter quite free of charge

parts.words: A little matter quite free of charge
parts.note: a tiny particle of matter with no electrical charge, read as a small affair that costs nothing

explanation.surface: Something trivial that costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free of charge' suggests no cost; in physics it means electrically neutral.
explanation.definitionFit: This subatomic particle has no electric charge.

clue.text: Give up and return

explanation.surface: Surrender and go back.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender is to cede; an investment's income is its output.

clue.text: The cruelty one would expect to find in 5 countries?

definitions.text: The cruelty one would expect to find in 5 countries?

parts.words: The cruelty one would expect to find in 5 countries?
parts.note: lands short of people would be short of mankind, which also means inhumane behaviour

explanation.surface: A suggestion that sparsely peopled lands are heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 is 5-down, UNDERPOPULATED: such countries lack people, i.e. mankind.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhumane conduct shows an absence of compassion, the literal shortage of people.

clue.text: Dad holding a high card that can solve all problems

indicators.note: the word for dad holds the other piece inside it, as a hand holds a card

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
an ace is the top card in many games

explanation.surface: Father keeps an ace up his sleeve to fix everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A cure-all remedy is supposed to fix every difficulty.

clue.text: Disagreement between men put in wrong side

indicators.note: one word is placed in the middle of the scrambled other
the letters of side are put the wrong way, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A quarrel among men placed on the wrong team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Between men' belongs to the definition; 'wrong' rearranges the letters of 'side', and 'in' sets 'put' inside that scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel or argument is a clash of views between people.

clue.text: Business decision clinched near Dover

definitions.meaning: A Kent coastal town a few miles north of Dover

explanation.surface: A business agreement signed somewhere close to Dover.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinched bargain is an agreement; the Kent town lies beside Dover.

clue.text: The characteristic sound of piped music

definitions.text: The characteristic sound of piped music

parts.words: The characteristic sound of piped music
parts.note: the shrill wail of Scottish bagpipes, not background music in shops

explanation.surface: A comment on the sound of background music in shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piped music' suggests muzak; here it is music from bagpipes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots word names the shrill sound of bagpipes.

clue.text: Pointedly remind someone of quiet measure

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction to play softly
a rod is an old unit of length, five and a half yards

explanation.surface: Someone is nudged about a quiet unit.
explanation.definitionFit: To poke or nudge someone as a reminder is to jog them.

clue.text: Kind of chocolate found all over Lombardy

definitions.meaning: the Po valley flatland covers much of Lombardy

explanation.surface: A chocolate on sale throughout northern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark chocolate is sold under this name; Lombardy is largely flat lowland.

clue.text: Begintoshowsignofner vousness

definitions.meaning: printed run together, it reads 'to show sign of nervousness': to jump in fright

explanation.surface: Starting to look jittery.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is printed with its spaces lost: read it as 'Begin to show sign of nervousness'.
explanation.definitionFit: To commence; also to jump in alarm.

clue.text: In its turn it may bring success or ruin

definitions.text: In its turn it may bring success or ruin

parts.words: In its turn it may bring success or ruin
parts.note: a spinning device of fate whose rotation brings good or bad luck

explanation.surface: A remark that whatever happens next can make or break you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In its turn' sounds like 'in due course', but literally means as it rotates.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval emblem of fate is a spinning disc raising and lowering people.

clue.text: The Spartan who was mainly successful in winning over the Athenians

definitions.text: The Spartan who was mainly successful in winning over the Athenians

parts.words: The Spartan who was mainly successful in winning over the Athenians
parts.note: the Spartan admiral who defeated Athens at sea to end the Peloponnesian War

explanation.surface: A Spartan leader who triumphed over Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' means at sea (the main): his victory at Aegospotami was naval.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spartan admiral's naval win at Aegospotami in 405 BC ended the war.

clue.text: A response of doubtful validity

parts.note: an answer that can be read in more than one way, so its meaning is uncertain

explanation.surface: A reply whose truth is questionable.
explanation.definitionFit: An equivocal answer has unclear meaning, so its worth is uncertain.

clue.text: Is pursuing me with speed in the state of Tennessee

indicators.note: one piece follows behind the others, as a pursuer comes after

parts.note: taken as written
mph, miles per hour, is a unit of speed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone rushes after me across Tennessee.
explanation.definitionFit: The city on the Mississippi lies in that southern US state.

clue.text: The mantle of sleep is

indicators.note: the mantle is made out of these letters, rearranged as raw material

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cloak worn for sleeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' marks the mantle as made from the letters of SLEEP IS, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A fur-trimmed cloak or cape worn over the shoulders.

clue.text: Ready to tackle any kind of sport

explanation.surface: Willing to play any sport going.
explanation.definitionFit: Up for anything means willing; a match or hunted animals are another sense.

clue.text: One who watches a medical substance being turned out?

indicators.note: turned out means shaken up into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
a drug is a medicine

explanation.surface: Someone watches as a medicine is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being turned out' rearranges A DRUG into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry keeps watch over people or places.

clue.text: Heathen god replete with silver

indicators.note: full of, so the god's name holds the other piece

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An idol crammed with silver.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-believer or idolater, outside the main religions.

clue.text: The 2 of 26

parts.note: 2-down's pen name, the alias used by 26-down

explanation.surface: A cross-reference puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 is PEN-NAME, 26 is LAMB: Charles Lamb wrote his essays under this pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb signed his Essays with this pseudonym.

clue.text: Nothing added to a blue dye

indicators.note: one piece is put on the end of the other

parts.note: nil means zero

explanation.surface: Nothing is mixed into a blue colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo plant yielding a blue colouring.

clue.text: Young skipper who won fame as an essayist

definitions.meaning: a baby sheep, which skips about

definitions.text: who won fame as an essayist

explanation.surface: A young captain became a famous writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skipper' suggests a ship's captain; it is an animal that skips.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby sheep frolics; Charles Lamb wrote the Essays of Elia.

clue.text: A West African tree insect I go after

indicators.note: the last piece follows the others

parts.note: the ash is a tree
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A tree insect in West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a Ghanaian people.

clue.text: Went by inordinately pleased

indicators.note: excessively, read as out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone passed by very happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has gone by has passed or slipped away, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Norfolk town holding drama shows

indicators.note: the town's name holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, an English county
a play is a drama

explanation.surface: A Norfolk town stages theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhibits or presentations.

clue.text: Dim and watery section of an invincible army

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tired part of an unbeatable army.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleary eyes are dim-sighted and moist.
